# demo-app

A small, mostly-secure Flask service used to showcase the `vulnreach`
reachability engine. This is a **defensive-security demo fixture**: there is no
exploit code anywhere in it. The only thing "vulnerable" about the app is that a
few dependency *versions* in `requirements.txt` are intentionally outdated.

The point of the fixture is to show the difference between *having* an outdated
dependency and *being able to reach it* from a public HTTP route.

## What the service does

A notes/config/report API with three public HTTP routes:

| Method & path            | Handler                                  | What it reaches                        |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| `POST /configs/import`   | `controllers.config_controller.import_config` | PyYAML (parses an uploaded YAML config) |
| `GET  /reports/<id>`     | `controllers.report_controller.get_report`    | Jinja2 (renders a report to HTML)       |
| `GET  /health`           | `controllers.health_controller.health`        | requests (checks an upstream service)   |

All three routes are **public** (registered as blueprints on the app in
`app.py`); there is no auth layer in this demo.

## Architecture

The code is layered so that the call chains are genuinely multi-file and
several hops deep:

```
app.py                      Flask app; registers the blueprints below
controllers/                HTTP blueprints (the public entry points)
  config_controller.py        POST /configs/import
  report_controller.py        GET  /reports/<id>
  health_controller.py        GET  /health
services/                   business logic
  config_service.py           ingest -> validation_service
  validation_service.py       validate -> yaml_parser
  report_service.py           build_report -> content_service
  content_service.py          assemble -> template_service
  template_service.py         render -> html_renderer
  health_service.py           check_upstream -> requests.get
parsers/                    request-body parsing
  yaml_parser.py              parse -> loader
  loader.py                   load_document -> yaml.load   (PyYAML)
renderers/
  html_renderer.py            render_html -> jinja2.escape (Jinja2)
maintenance/                offline jobs (NOT wired to any route)
  sync.py                     run_sync (cron/CLI only)
  http.py                     fetch -> urllib3            (urllib3)
tools/

info:
  title: demo-app API
  version: "1.0.0"
  description: >
    Public HTTP API for the demo-app reachability fixture. All three routes are
    public and unauthenticated: there is no login, API key or token layer, so
    any client can call every endpoint. Configuration records and rendered
    reports are persisted in PostgreSQL via SQLAlchemy, a Redis cache fronts
    report rendering, and the health probe calls an upstream status service over
    HTTP with the requests client.
servers:
  - url: http://localhost:5000
    description: Local development server
paths:
  /configs/import:
    post:
      operationId: import_config
      summary: Import a YAML configuration document
      description: >
        Accepts user-supplied YAML in the request body and ingests it. The raw
        bytes flow through the config service (`ingest`) into the validation
        service (`validate`) and the YAML parser (`load_document`), which parses
        the document with PyYAML. The accepted document is stored as a config
        record in PostgreSQL via SQLAlchemy. This endpoint is public and
        unauthenticated.
      requestBody:
        required: true
        description: The raw YAML configuration document to import.
        content:
          application/x-yaml:
            schema:
              type: string
              example: |
                name: example
                retries: 3
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Number of top-level keys imported.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  imported:
                    type: integer
  /reports/{report_id}:
    get:
      operationId: get_report
      summary: Render a stored report as HTML
      description: >
        Loads the report row identified by `report_id` from PostgreSQL (through
        SQLAlchemy, with a Redis cache in front to avoid re-rendering repeat
        requests) and renders it to an HTML fragment. Untrusted report fields are
        escaped through Jinja2 in the renderer before they reach the page. Public
        and unauthenticated.
      parameters:
        - name: report_id
          in: path
          required: true
          description: Caller-controlled identifier of the report to render.
          schema:
            type: string
      responses:
        "200":
          description: An HTML fragment for the report.
          conten

HTTP controllers (Flask blueprints) for the demo service.

module-level function so the reachability engine can follow the call chain from
